raw_response:
Alright, let me think this through as I sit here planning out the year.

---

**My thinking, in my own voice:**

I've been working this same 7.8 mu for 40 years. Wheat in the winter, corn in the summer, that's how we do it here in Quzhou. It's just me and the wife now — kids are in town, they don't come back to help with the fields anymore. So whatever I can't do with my own hands, I pay someone with a tractor to come do it.

7.8 mu isn't a big piece of land. I can't waste money. But I also can't skimp too much — if I put down too little fertilizer the wheat turns yellow and the yield drops, then I've lost more than I saved. Old Wang next to me tried cutting back two years ago and his yield fell maybe 50 kg per mu. Not worth it.

**Wheat first.** After the corn comes off in early October, I'll get the ground plowed — I pay the tractor man about 40 yuan per mu. Then plant around October 12-15, that's when everyone in the village plants. I buy the common seed from the shop in town, Jimai or Shimai something, whatever they have — costs me around 4 yuan per jin and I seed maybe 15 kg per mu. Before planting I put down one and a half bags of the 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu, that's 75 kg. Then in spring when it greens up I spread urea, about 15 kg per mu across the field.

I water the wheat 3 times usually — once before winter to put it to sleep good, once at green-up in March, once at jointing in April. If the spring is dry I do a fourth at grain-filling, but the pump eats electricity so I only do it if I have to. I spray herbicide once in spring because at 61 I can't be pulling weeds by hand, and once against aphids if I see them bad. Last few years my wheat has given me around 400-420 kg per mu, so I plan on 400.

**Then the corn, right after.** The wheat comes off around June 8-12, and I've got maybe 3-4 days to get corn in. No time to plow — I hire the no-till seeder, the fellow with the red tractor does it for 30 yuan per mu and he drops seed and compound fertilizer in one pass. I use Xianyu 335 or whatever hybrid the shop pushes that year, about 30 yuan of seed per mu. Compound fertilizer at planting, 50 kg per mu. Then when the corn is knee-high in July I go through with urea, about 20 kg per mu, spread by hand — that's still something I can do.

Corn water depends on the sky. If July-August gives us rain, I don't water at all. If it's dry I run the well once or twice. Last year I watered twice. I get maybe 470-500 kg per mu on corn in a normal year.

My biggest worry is the labor — my back isn't what it was. And the electricity for pumping keeps going up. But I'll do what I've always done. It works.
